author: Laxmann, 1769
status: 나그네새 수만 마리 · 여름철새 수천 마리
summary: 도시나 농촌의 인가 주변에 살며 전국에서 번식하는 흔한 여름철새이다. 이동할 때나 번식 초기에는 암수가 함께 또는 홀로 지내고, 번식이 끝나면 가족끼리 몰려다니는 일이 많다. 처마 밑이나 다리 밑, 지붕 밑에 흔히 무리 지어 긴 술병을 옆으로 눕힌 듯한 둥지를 짓고, 5~7월에 알을 4~5개 낳는다. 국외에서는 남유럽과 아시아 온대 지역에서 번식하고 동남아시아, 아프리카, 인도에서 겨울을 난다.

art.subject: Eastern Red-rumped Swallow (Cecropis daurica), adult (sexes alike), as seen in Korean villages from April to September: crown, mantle, scapulars and back glossy purplish blue-black; a rufous-orange patch behind the eye extending onto the sides of the nape; rump broadly rufous-orange with fine dark streaks; uppertail coverts blue-black; underparts from chin to belly pale buff to pale rufous with fine dark streaks; long undertail coverts blue-glossed black, so the tail looks dipped in ink from below; tail deeply forked and blackish, the outer streamers very long and without white spots. Bill tiny, black. Dark brown eye. Dark brown legs.
art.pose: in flight, banking to show the rusty-red rump and long outer tail feathers
art.scene: Korean summer countryside: open fields and a stream near a rural village; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view perched on a wire: glossy blue-black crown and back, rufous-orange nape sides and rump, finely streaked pale buff underparts, black undertail coverts, long forked tail
adult in flight seen from above, head, body and tail in one line: rufous-orange rump band contrasting with blue-black back, wings and forked tail
adult in flight seen from below: finely streaked buff underparts, square-cut black undertail coverts, long outer tail streamers without white spots
art.build: Swallow slightly larger and stockier than Barn Swallow, with broader-based wings. Bill tiny with a wide gape. Legs very short, dark. Tail deeply forked, the outer streamers about two and a half times the length of the central feathers and slightly curving inward. Flight slower and more gliding than Barn Swallow's, often sailing on flat wings. Perches on wires and builds a bottle-shaped mud nest with a long entrance tunnel under eaves and bridges.
avoid: Do not paint a dark red throat and blue-black breast band — that is Barn Swallow (Hirundo rustica).
Do not paint white spots in the tail (Barn Swallow).
Do not paint a white rump (Asian House Martin) or unstreaked white underparts.
Do not paint a short, shallow-forked tail; the outer streamers are very long.
